newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle market quiet - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle market quiet - feedlots.

text.p: CHICAGO, June 6 Reuter) - U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets early Friday were quiet, with no reported bids or sales following active movement that set a weekly record high in Kansas, feedlot sources said.
Sales on Thursday were thin at $63.00 per cwt, down $1.00 from the bulk of this week's sales and down $2.00 from the majority of cattle that sold last week, they said.
This week's brisk activity sold out most showlists, but projections for large cattle supplies were seen resulting in packers dropping bids to $62.00 early next week, sources said.
Fed cattle prices next week also could be pressured by slow packer demand following this week's heavy sales, which more than covered nearby packer needs, feedlot sources said.
Demand for fed cattle also could be dampened by light retail demand, with most retail coolers well stocked with beef going into the Father's Day weekend, Sunday June 15, the sources said.
Beef movement this week was strong, but packers had to lower prices to entice the sales.
